summary: The whole of the record: Wilde's inscription in a copy of his Poems calling Isidore de Lara 'the poet of the musicians, in sincere admiration and affection'.
certainty_reasoning: The record documents a friendship or acquaintance with no evidence of attraction or romance; classified platonic, upgradable if contrary evidence comes to light.

sources.quote: To my friend Isidore de Lara, the poet of the musicians, in sincere admiration and affection, Oscar Wilde, June '87.
sources.context: Wilde's inscription in a copy of his Poems (fifth edition, 1882), recorded by the editors in a note on de Lara's opera, produced at Monte Carlo under the patronage of Princess Alice of Monaco. Not a letter: no correspondence between them survives. The editors point to Osbert Sitwell's Noble Essences (1950) for a portrait.
sources.speaker: Oscar Wilde
sources.supports: The whole of the record: one inscription, in Wilde's hand, calling him a friend.
sources.citation_provenance: PDF p. 1182. The editors record the inscription's wording but not where the book is - note 2 says only "There exists a copy of Wilde's Poems (fifth edition, 1882) inscribed" - so no repository can be written for it.

sources.context: London is believed to be where the inscription was written - Wilde lived there when the fifth edition of Poems was current - but no source in this record names the city: the note records the inscription's text and the opera produced at Monte Carlo, not where the book was inscribed.
sources.locator: General Index s.v. de Lara, Isidore
sources.supports: Would settle London as where the inscription was written: the volume's de Lara index entry, read at the page.
